title: KOJI FIZZ — New York Edition
jpTitle: KOJI FIZZ — ブランドプロモーションフィルム
summary: A short-film series for a new Japanese prebiotic drink, told through real New York creatives in their own studios — unscripted. I ran the client side and the creative intent: the concept, who the story should be about, the director we hired. The director and crew made the films.

angles.creative: Instead of an ad, a portrait: four short films where New York creatives talk about how they work, with the product in the room rather than in the script. I shaped the concept, chose the director and decided whose stories these would be.
angles.leadership: Client-facing creative production between a Japanese brand owner, a New York agency and a film crew: translating the brand's intent into a brief, selecting the director, and keeping a small production pointed at one story.

mine: Client communication with the agency and the brand owner
Helping shape the overall concept — creatives in their own environments, no scripts
Selecting and hiring the film director
Deciding who the story should focus on
Shaping the narrative of each short story
Guiding creative intention with the director and production team
Scouting and coordinating on-location filming across studios
team: T.J. Misny — film director: directed and shot the films
Akifumi Yamada (Morinaga & Co.) — KOJI FIZZ inventor; Masato Nagumo — packaging designer

metrics.label: films — a compilation and three portraits

narrative.situation: Morinaga's prebiotic drink KOJI FIZZ was launching in New York through the agency See the Sun.
narrative.problem: The brand wanted genuine creative endorsement rather than a traditional advertising campaign.
built: KOJI FIZZ New York Edition — compilation film

business: The series became central to the brand's promotion strategy.
